messages.subject: Both defects scoped in one proposal; repo cleaned up
messages.body: Cleaned up all six scratch files from the repo root (git status now shows only the two accepted files, ingest.py and test_ingest.py, plus your untracked .orca/), and wrote a single proposal covering both remaining splitter defects with no code changed. I found the two defects are NOT one shared rule: the Privacy Act's endnote table and a real cross-reference table inside Legal Profession Uniform Law Application Act 2022 (WA) are both dense, tightly-packed runs of heading-shaped lines (median gap ~144 chars vs ~1,406 for real Part IIIC sections) that a generalised, already-validated density check (extending CONTENTS_MIN_ENTRIES beyond just the document preamble) would catch cleanly and non-regressively -- but case-law footnote/exhibit lines (Hill v Van Erp, ACCC v George Weston Foods) are isolated, non-clustering lookalikes that this density rule can't catch, and I argue that one needs a document-type-level decision (does case law get provisions at all) rather than another splitter tweak. The proposal gives both defects real sourced fixtures with explicit non-regression cases, states the blast radius and that the density fix should land before any re-ingest, and leaves the case-law scope decision and the re-ingest go/no-go to the owner.
